title: Responsive & cross-browser polish for Console tables, charts, and modals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Finish final responsive layout pass and cross-browser polish for key Redwood Console pages: Routes table, Model Usage dashboard charts, and rollout modal. This ticket consolidates prototype feedback, captures remaining visual/interaction edge cases across breakpoints, and specifies acceptance criteria for engineering handoff.

Scope:
- Tables: Routes & Tokens list (row density, column priority collapse behavior, sticky headers, keyboard navigation).
- Charts: Per-route latency histogram, cost breakdown stacked bar, time-series sparkline mini-charts (focus on pixel-alignment and tooltip behavior across DPRs).
- Modals: Rollout modal (canary sliders), Confirm Delete modal, and Compose API key modal (responsive form flow and focus trap).
- Cross-browser: Chrome, Firefox, Safari (macOS & iOS), Edge. Emphasis on font rendering, subpixel rounding for chart axes, and position of sticky elements during mobile viewport resize.

Key outcomes:
1) Finalized breakpoint rules and column collapse priorities for tables.
2) Resolved SVG/chart rendering differences across browsers (canvas fallback where needed).
3) Polished modal stacking + focus management for mobile and small desktops.
4) Accessibility checks: keyboard order, ARIA for dynamic tables, color contrast for stacked bars.

Artifacts & links:
- Figma master file (responsive frames & components): https://www.figma.com/file/RwConsole/console-responsive-v2 (prototype page: "Responsive — March")
- Clickable prototype (flows for table collapse & rollout modal): https://figma.link/RwConsoleProtoMar
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/UX/Console+Responsive+Guidelines
- Demo recording of problematic Safari rendering (obs): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1safarirepro
- Engineering PR for initial table responsive behavior: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1427

Trade-offs & notes:
- We experimented with fluid column reordering vs. column collapse. Decided to use collapse-to-row pattern for P0 columns to avoid heavy JS reflow and to maintain keyboard ordering. This increases vertical space on narrow viewports but keeps data readable.
- For charts, we prefer SVG for accessibility/DOM tooltips, but Safari 2x DPR bug with subpixel axis lines forces a dual rendering path: SVG in Chrome/Edge/Firefox, and a lightweight Canvas fallback for Safari mobile where pixel alignment is critical. Engineering has an experimental feature flag (ENG-3198) to toggle canvas fallback.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Tables: at 1200px/900px/720px/420px breakpoints the Routes table shows column collapse in the order defined in Figma; sticky header remains visible; keyboard navigation (arrow keys + enter to open row actions) works in Chrome/Firefox/Safari.
- Charts: latency histogram and stacked cost bars render without vertical axis aliasing in all target browsers on 1x and 2x DPR; tooltip anchor should not clip at viewport edges and should be fully keyboard accessible.
- Modals: rollout modal keeps focus trap when opened from a table action in narrow view; form fields stack in a logical order at <720px and Save/Cancel actions are reachable without horizontal scroll.
- Accessibility: color contrast for all chart segments >= WCAG AA; table rows announce summary text when focused (screen reader testing notes attached).

Handoff notes for engineering:
- Component list: ResponsiveTable, StickyHeader, CollapsibleColumns, ChartWrapper (svg/canvas switch), ModalStackManager, FocusTrap. See Figma component names and tokens for spacing scales.
- Tokens: use spacing-scale-2/3/4 for mobile/tablet/desktop row padding; typography token map in Confluence.
- Performance: prefer CSS transforms for sticky behaviors; avoid layout-thrashing listeners. Batching resize handlers and using ResizeObserver recommended.

QA checklist (for design & QA to sign off):
- [ ] Verify column collapse order at listed breakpoints in Chrome/Firefox/Safari
- [ ] Replay Safari rendering repro and verify canvas path improves axis alignment
- [ ] Keyboard-only pass on tables and modals
- [ ] Screen reader summary text validation on focused table rows
- [ ] Mobile orientation and pinch-zoom behavior does not break sticky elements

Risks & open questions:
- Canvas fallback increases maintenance; we should track usage telemetry to evaluate long-term viability. (See ENG-3198).
- Potential conflicts with Dedicated console layout if customer-specific columns are injected; need to ensure collapse rules are pluggable.

Next steps:
- Design to merge final Figma frames and update component tokens (due 2026-03-14).
- Engineering to implement canvas fallback behind flag and iterate on ResizeObserver debounce (ENG-3198, ENG-3124).
- Schedule a cross-browser QA block for 3 days after PR merge.

Summary: This ticket completes a design-to-handoff cycle for responsive and cross-browser polish across high-impact Console pages. The focus is pragmatic: keep interactions predictable, prioritize accessibility, and add minimal interoperability fallbacks for platform/browser quirks.
acceptance_criteria: Tables collapse/collapse-to-row behavior matches Figma at 1200/900/720/420px in Chrome/Firefox/Safari
Sticky headers persist and do not overlap action menus on resize
Charts render axis lines and tooltips correctly at 1x and 2x DPR across target browsers
Rollout and Confirm modals maintain focus trap and proper stacking order on mobile
Keyboard navigation and screen reader announcements verified for tables
ux_decisions: Use collapse-to-row pattern for low-priority columns instead of reordering to preserve keyboard order
Prefer SVG for charts, but enable canvas fallback for Safari 2x DPR subpixel issues
Sticky header implemented via CSS transform with ResizeObserver to adjust offset when banner shown
testing_plan: Cross-browser visual regression: capture screenshots at 1200/900/720/420px in Chrome/Firefox/Safari (macOS + iOS)
Keyboard-only walkthrough across all table actions and modal flows
Screen reader (VoiceOver + NVDA) checks for focused row summaries
Performance smoke test for initial table render under 1000 rows with virtualization enabled
